summary: Yulian Zeng is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University, where he was supervised by Kirill Solonin, and also studied under the traditional teacher Hsing Yun.
Yumi Katayama works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. She studied as a PhD student at Hiroshima University (attested 2007) and under supervisor Kenyu Mitomo (attested 2013).

Yumi Nakamoto works in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. She studied at Ryukoku University as a graduate research student (attested 2014) and served there as an open-recruitment researcher in 2012.
Yumiko Ishihama is a scholar in Tibetology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Waseda University from circa 1980 to 1989 and later held an academic post there around 1999.

Yun Ji specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed a PhD in Chinese literature at Fudan University by 2006 and held the post of librarian at the Buddhist College of Singapore (attested 2015).
Yungfen Ma specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She earned a PhD at Columbia University under the doctoral supervision of Chün-fang Yü (attested 2011).
Yunxi Wang was a Sinology scholar who studied at Fudan University from circa 1947 to 1951. He subsequently held a post at Fudan University from circa 1951 until his death in 2014.

Yuri Levada studied philosophy at Moscow University (~1947–1952). He held posts at Moscow State University and the Institute of Sociology (~1966–1972), VTSIOM (~1988–2003), Levada Center (~2003–2006), and the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences.
Yuri Parfionovich was a scholar in the field of Tibetology. He pursued his studies under teacher George de Roerich and traditional teacher Bidia Dandaron.
Yusen Kashiwahara was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Otani University from circa 1937 to 1941 and later served as a professor there from circa 1952 to 1987.

Yusho Miyasaka studied at Chisan College and Tohoku University under Shoko Watanabe. In Buddhist studies and Indology, he taught at Koyasan University, served as Professor Emeritus at Nagoya University, and held posts at Chisan Denpōin and Shuchiin University.

Yusho Wakahara specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University under Esho Mikogami, lectured at Hanazono University (attested 1987), and served as assistant professor and professor at Ryukoku University.
Yutai Ikeda was a Buddhist studies scholar who held a post at Otani University and served as Emeritus Professor at Doho University from circa 1969 to 2005.

Yutaka Hirata specialized in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology, receiving a doctorate from Kyushu University (~1996). He worked at Nara National Research Institute for Cultural Properties, became Professor Emeritus at Kyushu University, and was a professor at Nagasaki Junshin Catholic University.

Yutaka Iwamoto studied Indology and Buddhist studies at Kyoto University (~1930–1933) under Toru Haneda and Hidenaka Tanaka. He held professorships at Tokai, Kyoto Tachibana, and Soka Universities, and Tokyo University of Science, after lecturing at Kyoto University.

Yutaka Kanazawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at Ryukoku University by 2010, supervised by Shoryu Katsura and Masaaki Noni, and also studied under Kōgi Kudara, Hōgei Mitsukawa, and Isao Shimizu.

Yutaka Kawasaki is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Seio Okuda. He holds affiliations at the University of Tokyo (attested 2024), International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Yutaka Ochihara studied Indology and linguistics at Kyoto University and the University of Pennsylvania. He studied under Atsuuji Ashikaga, Louis Renou, W. Norman Brown, and Armand Minard, holding professorships at Kyoto University and the Collège de France.

Yutaka Takagi is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Tokyo University of Literature and Science from circa 1948 to 1951 and was a professor at Rissho University from circa 1974 to 1999.

Yutaka Yoshida studied at Tokyo University of Education, Hitotsubashi University, and the University of Tokyo. He held several posts at Hitotsubashi University, becoming Professor Emeritus in 2018, and served at Kyoto University from circa 2006 to 2020.
